gap: No result ChatGPT got names a third-party charger confirmed to have the S26 Ultra's 20 V PPS profile. Charge-Test (Michael Barton, 2026-03-09) lists nine by name, among them the Anker Prime 160W (A2687), which sells for $99.99 at anker.com today against $54.99 for Samsung's own 60W adapter at samsung.com.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT got. Android Authority says 'Third-party options are available, but it's not always clear if they support Samsung's required 20V mode' and names none. The SamMobile 60W article names only 'Samsung's newly launched 60W charger'. The SamMobile Trio article names only the Trio (fails) and the EP-T6010 at $54.99. ChargerLAB's compatibility page has a text intro only; its results are in the embedded video. GSMArena's 67W third-party charger is unnamed (the page returned 402 to me; ChatGPT's answer and Samscopes both say it is unnamed). ChatGPT said outright that it 'couldn't verify a specific third-party retail model'. Charge-Test's named list fills that gap. It is not a 3 because Charge-Test does not publish per-charger watts or times, so the list proves the PPS range, not a measured S26 result per model.
decides: The overall pick stays the same: Samsung's 60W adapter is the only charger with a named, measured S26 Ultra result (Android Authority: 60 W peak for about 2 minutes, about 48 W sustained, 42 minutes to full). The finding sets up a 'multi-port / laptop too' segment. Our listed Anker Prime 160W is on Charge-Test's confirmed list (PPS 4.5–21 V at 5 A), so it can honestly win as the one charger that does the S26 Ultra's top mode and a 140 W laptop. Price today: $99.99 at anker.com, marked down from $149.99; Amazon blocked the check. The Samsung 65W Trio is the well-known charger that fails: its PPS stops at 20 V / 2.25 A, which is 45 W (SamMobile). Charge-Test also puts numbers on why 'PPS' alone is not enough: a 5–11 V / 5 A PPS charger gave 42.9 W, 5–16 V / 3 A gave 38.2 W, and the wide-range PPS charger gave 53–54 W.

findings.label: Charger requirement for the S26 Ultra's 60 W mode
findings.value: USB PD 3.1 with PPS and 20 V / 3 A from a single port; the bundled 3 A cable is enough and a 5 A cable does not charge faster

findings.label: S26 Ultra peak by PPS profile (Charge-Test)
findings.value: Wide-range PPS 5–21 V / 5 A: about 53–54 W peak at 16.5–18.5 V; PPS 5–11 V / 5 A: 42.9 W; PPS 5–16 V / 3 A: 38.2 W; no PPS: 14.5 W (20 W charger) / 22.3 W (100 W charger)
findings.source_title: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra charging speed test: SFC 3.0 / PPS - Charge-Test
findings.note: Also 51% at 15 minutes with SFC 3.0 vs 49% with SFC 2.0, and about 62 minutes 5–100% in both modes. That conflicts with Android Authority's 60 W peak and 42 minutes, so the page should give both with their names.
